A: Under sub-section (2), the Sessions Judge shall determine by order in writing the Judge who shall be deemed to be the successor-in-office. [Source: Section 29, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Powers of Judges and Magistrates exercisable by their successors-in office

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 29: Powers of Judges and Magistrates exercisable by their successors-in office

Q: What condition applies if there is doubt as to who is the successor to a Magistrate?
A: Under sub-section (3), the Chief Judicial Magistrate, or the District Magistrate, as the case may be, shall determine by order in writing the Magistrate who shall be deemed to be the successor. [Source: Section 29, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Powers of Judges and Magistrates exercisable by their successors-in office

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 29: Powers of Judges and Magistrates exercisable by their successors-in office

Q: Are the rules allowing a successor to exercise a Judge's powers completely unconditioned?
A: No, under sub-section (1), this allowance is "Subject to the other provisions of this Sanhita." [Source: Section 29, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Powers of Judges and Magistrates exercisable by their successors-in office

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 29: Powers of Judges and Magistrates exercisable by their successors-in office

Q: What is the consequence of the Chief Judicial Magistrate issuing a written order naming a successor?
A: The consequence is that the named Magistrate is legally authorized to take over any proceedings or orders left pending by the previous Magistrate, ensuring cases do not stall. [Source: Section 29, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Powers of Judges and Magistrates exercisable by their successors-in office

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 30: Powers of superior officers of police

Q: Can a high-ranking police official exercise the same powers as a local station head?
A: Police officers superior in rank to an officer in charge of a police station may exercise the same powers, throughout the local area to which they are appointed, as may be exercised by such officer within the limits of his station. [Source: Section 30, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Powers of superior officers of police

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 30: Powers of superior officers of police

Q: What does Section 30 of BNSS 2023 state?
A: Section 30 of BNSS 2023 grants superior police officers the authority to exercise the exact same powers as an officer in charge of a police station throughout their appointed local area. [Source: Section 30, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Powers of superior officers of police

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 30: Powers of superior officers of police

Q: A Superintendent of Police visits a local police station. Can the Superintendent perform an action that is normally reserved only for the officer in charge of that specific station?
A: Yes, as a police officer superior in rank, they may exercise the same powers throughout their local area as may be exercised by the officer in charge within the limits of his station. [Source: Section 30, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Powers of superior officers of police

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 30: Powers of superior officers of police

Q: What condition restricts where a superior police officer can exercise the powers of a station officer?
A: The superior officer may only exercise these powers "throughout the local area to which they are appointed." [Source: Section 30, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Powers of superior officers of police

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 30: Powers of superior officers of police

Q: Is a superior officer's power limited only to administrative tasks above the station level?
A: No, they may exercise "the same powers" as the officer in charge of the station. [Source: Section 30, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Powers of superior officers of police

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 30: Powers of superior officers of police

Q: What is the practical application of this section for a Deputy Inspector General overseeing several districts?
A: The consequence is that the DIG is legally empowered to step in and directly exercise the powers of any local station-house officer within those districts if necessary for an investigation. [Source: Section 30, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Powers of superior officers of police

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 31: Public when to assist Magistrates and police

Q: When is a normal citizen required to help the police or a Magistrate?
A: Every person is bound to assist a Magistrate or police officer reasonably demanding his aid in taking or preventing the escape of an authorized arrestee, preventing a breach of the peace, or preventing injury to public property. [Source: Section 31, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Public when to assist Magistrates and police

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 31: Public when to assist Magistrates and police

Q: What is Section 31 of BNSS 2023 about?
A: Section 31 of BNSS 2023 outlines the circumstances under which the general public is legally bound to assist Magistrates and police officers upon their reasonable demand. [Source: Section 31, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Public when to assist Magistrates and police

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 31: Public when to assist Magistrates and police

Q: A police officer is chasing a suspect they are authorized to arrest and yells for a nearby civilian to help stop the suspect's escape. Does the civilian have a legal duty to help?
A: Yes, under clause (a), every person is bound to assist a police officer reasonably demanding his aid in taking or preventing the escape of any other person whom such officer is authorised to arrest. [Source: Section 31, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Public when to assist Magistrates and police

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 31: Public when to assist Magistrates and police

Q: What condition triggers the public's duty to assist in these scenarios?
A: The Magistrate or police officer must be "reasonably demanding his aid." [Source: Section 31, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Public when to assist Magistrates and police

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 31: Public when to assist Magistrates and police

Q: Is the public bound to assist the police in investigating a financial crime under this specific section?
A: No, the duty specifically applies to arrests/escapes, preventing a breach of the peace, or preventing injury to public property. [Source: Section 31, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Public when to assist Magistrates and police

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 31: Public when to assist Magistrates and police

Q: What is the consequence if someone attempts to vandalize public property and a Magistrate demands civilian help?
A: The consequence is that under clause (c), every person present is legally bound to assist the Magistrate in the prevention of the injury attempted to be committed to that public property. [Source: Section 31, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Public when to assist Magistrates and police

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 32: Aid to person, other than police officer, executing warrant

Q: How can a private citizen help execute an arrest warrant if the warrant isn't directed to a police officer?
A: When a warrant is directed to a person other than a police officer, any other person may aid in the execution of such warrant if the person to whom it is directed is near at hand and acting in its execution. [Source: Section 32, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Aid to person, other than police officer, executing warrant

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 32: Aid to person, other than police officer, executing warrant

Q: What does Section 32 of BNSS 2023 state?
A: Section 32 of BNSS 2023 provides that any person may legally aid someone other than a police officer who is executing a warrant, provided the primary executor is present and acting. [Source: Section 32, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Aid to person, other than police officer, executing warrant

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 32: Aid to person, other than police officer, executing warrant

Q: A court directs an arrest warrant to a civilian. The civilian goes home and asks his friend to go across town and execute the warrant alone. Can the friend legally do this?
A: No, the friend may only aid in the execution if the person to whom the warrant is directed be "near at hand and acting in the execution of the warrant." [Source: Section 32, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Aid to person, other than police officer, executing warrant

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 32: Aid to person, other than police officer, executing warrant

Q: What are the two conditions required for a third party to aid a non-police officer in executing a warrant?
A: The person to whom the warrant is directed must be "near at hand" and "acting in the execution of the warrant." [Source: Section 32, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Aid to person, other than police officer, executing warrant

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 32: Aid to person, other than police officer, executing warrant

Q: Does this section give any person the authority to execute a warrant entirely on their own initiative?
A: No, it only permits any other person to "aid in the execution of such warrant" under the specified conditions. [Source: Section 32, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Aid to person, other than police officer, executing warrant

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 32: Aid to person, other than police officer, executing warrant

Q: What is the practical application of this rule for a person named to execute a warrant?
A: The consequence is that the named person can legally enlist the physical assistance of bystanders or friends during the actual moment of arrest, as long as they themselves remain present and involved. [Source: Section 32, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Aid to person, other than police officer, executing warrant

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 33: Public to give information of certain offences

Q: What is the legal duty of a citizen who learns someone is planning to commit murder?
A: Every person aware of the intention of any other person to commit an offence like murder must forthwith give information to the nearest Magistrate or police officer. [Source: Section 33, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Public to give information of certain offences

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 33: Public to give information of certain offences

Q: What is Section 33 of BNSS 2023 about?
A: Section 33 of BNSS 2023 lists specific serious offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and imposes a strict legal duty on the public to report the commission or intention of these crimes to authorities. [Source: Section 33, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Public to give information of certain offences

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 33: Public to give information of certain offences

Q: A citizen learns about an offence covered under section 307 of the BNS that was committed by an Indian in another country. Do they still have to report it locally?
A: Yes, under sub-section (2), the term "offence" includes any act committed at any place out of India which would constitute an offence if committed in India. [Source: Section 33, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Public to give information of certain offences

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 33: Public to give information of certain offences

Q: What condition triggers the duty to report under this section?
A: The duty is triggered when a person becomes aware of the commission of, or of the intention of any other person to commit, any of the specifically enumerated offences. [Source: Section 33, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Public to give information of certain offences

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 33: Public to give information of certain offences

Q: Are citizens required by this section to report absolutely every minor traffic violation or petty theft they witness?
A: No, the duty to report is limited only to the specific, serious offences listed under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in clauses (i) through (xii). [Source: Section 33, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Public to give information of certain offences

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 33: Public to give information of certain offences

Q: What is the immediate procedural consequence required of a person who witnesses a kidnapping (section 140)?
A: The consequence is that they must "forthwith give information to the nearest Magistrate or police officer" regarding that commission. [Source: Section 33, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Public to give information of certain offences

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 34: Duty of officers employed in connection with affairs of a village to make certain report

Q: What are the reporting obligations of a village headman regarding suspicious deaths?
A: Every officer employed in connection with the affairs of a village shall forthwith communicate to the nearest Magistrate or police station any information he possesses regarding the occurrence of any sudden, unnatural, or suspicious death near the village. [Source: Section 34, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Duty of officers employed in connection with affairs of a village to make certain report

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 34: Duty of officers employed in connection with affairs of a village to make certain report

Q: What does Section 34 of BNSS 2023 cover?
A: Section 34 of BNSS 2023 mandates village officers and residents to quickly report specific criminal activities, suspicious deaths, the presence of proclaimed offenders, or threats to public order to the nearest Magistrate or police station. [Source: Section 34, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Duty of officers employed in connection with affairs of a village to make certain report

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 34: Duty of officers employed in connection with affairs of a village to make certain report

Q: A villager knows that an escaped convict is hiding out in an abandoned building within their village lands. Who must they report this to?
A: Under clause (b) of sub-section (1), they must forthwith communicate this information to "the nearest Magistrate or to the officer in charge of the nearest police station, whichever is nearer." [Source: Section 34, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Duty of officers employed in connection with affairs of a village to make certain report

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 34: Duty of officers employed in connection with affairs of a village to make certain report

Q: What specific conditions regarding stolen property trigger a reporting requirement under this section?
A: Under clause (a) of sub-section (1), information respecting the "permanent or temporary residence of any notorious receiver or vendor of stolen property in or near such village" must be reported. [Source: Section 34, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Duty of officers employed in connection with affairs of a village to make certain report

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 34: Duty of officers employed in connection with affairs of a village to make certain report

Q: Is the term "village" restricted strictly to the residential settlement area?
A: No, under clause (i) of sub-section (2), "village" includes village lands. [Source: Section 34, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Duty of officers employed in connection with affairs of a village to make certain report

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 34: Duty of officers employed in connection with affairs of a village to make certain report

Q: What is the legal consequence for a Panchayat member who hears a rumor of an intended riot affecting village safety?
A: Under clause (f) of sub-section (1), if the District Magistrate has directed them to communicate such matters, they are legally obligated to report it forthwith. [Source: Section 34, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Duty of officers employed in connection with affairs of a village to make certain report

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 35: When police may arrest without warrant

Q: Under what circumstances can the police make an arrest without a judicial warrant?
A: A police officer may arrest a person without a warrant if they commit a cognizable offence in the officer's presence, are suspected of a serious cognizable offence, are a proclaimed offender, or obstruct an officer, among other specific conditions. [Source: Section 35, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: When police may arrest without warrant

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 35: When police may arrest without warrant

Q: What is Section 35 of BNSS 2023 about?
A: Section 35 of BNSS 2023 details the specific scenarios, conditions, and procedures under which a police officer has the authority to arrest a person without an order from a Magistrate and without a warrant. [Source: Section 35, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: When police may arrest without warrant

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 35: When police may arrest without warrant

Q: A police officer receives a credible complaint that a suspect committed a cognizable offence punishable by four years in prison. The officer believes the suspect will tamper with evidence. Can the officer arrest the suspect without a warrant?
A: Yes, under clause (b) of sub-section (1), an arrest can be made for an offence punishable by less than seven years if the officer has reason to believe the person committed the offence and is satisfied the arrest is necessary to prevent tampering with evidence. [Source: Section 35, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: When police may arrest without warrant

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 35: When police may arrest without warrant

Q: What conditions must be satisfied to arrest someone without a warrant for an offence punishable by less than seven years?
A: Under clause (b) of sub-section (1), the officer must have reason to believe the person committed the offence and must be satisfied the arrest is necessary to prevent further offences, ensure proper investigation, prevent evidence tampering, prevent witness intimidation, or ensure court appearance, and must record reasons in writing. [Source: Section 35, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: When police may arrest without warrant

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 35: When police may arrest without warrant

Q: Can the police freely arrest an infirm person over sixty years of age without a warrant for a minor offence?
A: No, under sub-section (7), no arrest shall be made without prior permission of an officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police for offences punishable by less than three years if the person is infirm or above sixty. [Source: Section 35, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: When police may arrest without warrant

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 35: When police may arrest without warrant

Q: What happens if an arrest is not required for a person accused of a cognizable offence punishable by less than seven years?
A: Under sub-section (3), the consequence is that the police officer shall issue a notice directing the person to appear before him or at a specified place. [Source: Section 35, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: When police may arrest without warrant

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 36: Procedure of arrest and duties of officer making arrest

Q: What specific steps must a police officer follow when taking someone into custody?
A: Every police officer making an arrest must bear clear identification, prepare a memorandum of arrest attested by a witness and countersigned by the arrested person, and inform the person of their right to notify someone of the arrest. [Source: Section 36, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Procedure of arrest and duties of officer making arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 36: Procedure of arrest and duties of officer making arrest

Q: Can you explain Section 36 of BNSS 2023?
A: Section 36 of BNSS 2023 mandates the procedure and duties for an officer making an arrest, specifically requiring visible identification, a witness-attested memorandum of arrest, and notification of rights. [Source: Section 36, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Procedure of arrest and duties of officer making arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 36: Procedure of arrest and duties of officer making arrest

Q: An officer arrests a suspect and prepares an arrest memorandum. The officer has his partner witness and sign the memo. Is this legally sufficient?
A: No, under clause (b)(i), the memorandum must be attested by at least one witness "who is a member of the family of the person arrested or a respectable member of the locality where the arrest is made." [Source: Section 36, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Procedure of arrest and duties of officer making arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 36: Procedure of arrest and duties of officer making arrest

Q: What conditions apply to the identification a police officer must wear while making an arrest?
A: Under clause (a), the officer shall bear an accurate, visible, and clear identification of his name which will facilitate easy identification. [Source: Section 36, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Procedure of arrest and duties of officer making arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 36: Procedure of arrest and duties of officer making arrest

Q: Does the officer always have to verbally inform the arrested person of their right to notify a relative?
A: Under clause (c), they must inform the person of this right "unless the memorandum is attested by a member of his family." [Source: Section 36, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Procedure of arrest and duties of officer making arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 36: Procedure of arrest and duties of officer making arrest

Q: What is the documentary consequence of completing the arrest memorandum?
A: The consequence, under clause (b)(ii), is that the finalized document must be "countersigned by the person arrested" to validate the record of the procedure. [Source: Section 36, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Procedure of arrest and duties of officer making arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 37: Designated police officer

Q: How does the police department track and display information about people who have been arrested?
A: The State Government must establish police control rooms and designate an officer to maintain information about arrested persons, which must be prominently displayed at every police station and district headquarters. [Source: Section 37, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Designated police officer

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 37: Designated police officer

Q: What does Section 37 of BNSS 2023 mandate?
A: Section 37 of BNSS 2023 requires the establishment of police control rooms and the designation of a police officer responsible for maintaining and displaying records of arrested persons and their charges. [Source: Section 37, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Designated police officer

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 37: Designated police officer

Q: The State Government designates a Constable at the local station to be responsible for maintaining the database of arrested persons. Is this appointment valid under the Act?
A: No, under clause (b), the designated police officer must be "not below the rank of Assistant Sub-Inspector of Police." [Source: Section 37, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Designated police officer

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 37: Designated police officer

Q: What specific pieces of information must the designated police officer maintain about an arrested individual?
A: Under clause (b), they are responsible for maintaining information about the "names and addresses of the persons arrested" and the "nature of the offence with which charged." [Source: Section 37, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Designated police officer

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 37: Designated police officer

Q: Does this section dictate that the information of arrested persons must only be kept in a private logbook?
A: No, under clause (b), the information "shall be prominently displayed in any manner including in digital mode in every police station and at the district headquarters." [Source: Section 37, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Designated police officer

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 37: Designated police officer

Q: What is the infrastructural consequence of this section for the State Government?
A: The consequence, under clause (a), is that the State Government is legally compelled to "establish a police control room in every district and at State level." [Source: Section 37, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Designated police officer

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 38: Right of arrested person to meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation

Q: Does a suspect have the right to legal representation while being questioned by the police?
A: When any person is arrested and interrogated by the police, he shall be entitled to meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation, though not throughout the interrogation. [Source: Section 38, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Right of arrested person to meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 38: Right of arrested person to meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation

Q: What does Section 38 of BNSS 2023 state?
A: Section 38 of BNSS 2023 establishes the right of an arrested person to meet with an advocate of their choice during police interrogation, with the limitation that the advocate cannot be present for the entire duration. [Source: Section 38, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Right of arrested person to meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 38: Right of arrested person to meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation

Q: A suspect demands that their lawyer sit next to them and observe every single minute of a 5-hour police interrogation. Do the police have to allow this?
A: No, the section states the person is entitled to meet an advocate during interrogation, "though not throughout interrogation." [Source: Section 38, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Right of arrested person to meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 38: Right of arrested person to meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation

Q: What two conditions trigger the right granted by this section?
A: The right is triggered when any person is "arrested" and "interrogated by the police." [Source: Section 38, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Right of arrested person to meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 38: Right of arrested person to meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation

Q: Can the police assign a random state lawyer to the arrested person to satisfy this requirement?
A: No, the section explicitly states the arrested person is entitled to meet an advocate "of his choice." [Source: Section 38, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Right of arrested person to meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 38: Right of arrested person to meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation

Q: What is the procedural outcome when an arrested person requests to speak to their lawyer during questioning?
A: The consequence is that the police must grant the person a meeting with their advocate during the course of the interrogation, subject to the limitation that the advocate won't remain throughout. [Source: Section 38, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Right of arrested person to meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 39: Arrest on refusal to give name and residence

Q: Can a police officer arrest someone for a minor, non-cognizable offence just because they won't show ID?
A: If a person accused of committing a non-cognizable offence in an officer's presence refuses to give their name and residence, or gives a false one, the officer may arrest them to ascertain their true identity. [Source: Section 39, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest on refusal to give name and residence

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 39: Arrest on refusal to give name and residence

Q: What is Section 39 of BNSS 2023 about?
A: Section 39 of BNSS 2023 covers the procedure for arresting a person accused of a non-cognizable offence solely because they refuse to provide their true name and residence, and outlines their subsequent release. [Source: Section 39, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest on refusal to give name and residence

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 39: Arrest on refusal to give name and residence

Q: An officer arrests a tourist from another country for refusing to give their name after committing a non-cognizable offence. Once identified, can the tourist be released on a personal bond alone?
A: No, under the proviso to sub-section (2), if such person is not resident in India, the bail bond "shall be secured by a surety or sureties resident in India." [Source: Section 39, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest on refusal to give name and residence

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 39: Arrest on refusal to give name and residence

Q: What conditions must occur for a police officer to make an arrest under sub-section (1)?
A: The person must commit or be accused of a non-cognizable offence in the officer's presence, and must refuse on demand to give his name and residence or give information the officer has reason to believe is false. [Source: Section 39, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest on refusal to give name and residence

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 39: Arrest on refusal to give name and residence

Q: Is a person arrested under this section kept in custody indefinitely until their trial?
A: No, under sub-section (2), when their true name and residence have been ascertained, they "shall be released on a bond or bail bond, to appear before a Magistrate if so required." [Source: Section 39, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest on refusal to give name and residence

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 39: Arrest on refusal to give name and residence

Q: What is the consequence if the police cannot figure out the person's true identity within a day?
A: Under sub-section (3), if the true name and residence is not ascertained within twenty-four hours from the time of arrest, the person shall forthwith be forwarded to the nearest Magistrate having jurisdiction. [Source: Section 39, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest on refusal to give name and residence

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 40: Arrest by private person and procedure on such arrest

Q: Can an ordinary citizen perform an arrest under Indian law?
A: Any private person may arrest a person who in his presence commits a non-bailable and cognizable offence, or any proclaimed offender, and must hand them over to a police officer without unnecessary delay. [Source: Section 40, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest by private person and procedure on such arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 40: Arrest by private person and procedure on such arrest

Q: What does Section 40 of BNSS 2023 cover?
A: Section 40 of BNSS 2023 authorizes private persons to make arrests under specific serious conditions and outlines the immediate procedure for handing the arrested individual over to the police. [Source: Section 40, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest by private person and procedure on such arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 40: Arrest by private person and procedure on such arrest

Q: A shopkeeper sees a person commit a non-bailable, cognizable offence, arrests them, and locks them in a back room for 8 hours before calling the police. Is this lawful?
A: No, under sub-section (1), the private person must make over the arrested person to a police officer "without unnecessary delay, but within six hours from such arrest." [Source: Section 40, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest by private person and procedure on such arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 40: Arrest by private person and procedure on such arrest

Q: What conditions justify a private person making an arrest?
A: Under sub-section (1), the person must commit a "non-bailable and cognizable offence" in the private person's presence, or the person must be a "proclaimed offender." [Source: Section 40, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest by private person and procedure on such arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 40: Arrest by private person and procedure on such arrest

Q: Once the private person hands the suspect over to the police, does the suspect automatically go to jail?
A: Not necessarily; under sub-section (3), if there is no sufficient reason to believe the person has committed any offence, "he shall be at once released" by the police. [Source: Section 40, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest by private person and procedure on such arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 40: Arrest by private person and procedure on such arrest

Q: What is the consequence if the police take custody from the private person and find the suspect only committed a minor, non-cognizable offence?
A: Under sub-section (3), if the suspect refuses to give their true name and residence, they "shall be dealt with under the provisions of section 39." [Source: Section 40, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest by private person and procedure on such arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 41: Arrest by Magistrate

Q: Do Magistrates have the direct authority to arrest someone themselves?
A: Yes, when any offence is committed in the presence of a Magistrate within his local jurisdiction, he may himself arrest or order any person to arrest the offender. [Source: Section 41, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest by Magistrate

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 41: Arrest by Magistrate

Q: What is Section 41 of BNSS 2023 about?
A: Section 41 of BNSS 2023 details the powers of Executive and Judicial Magistrates to directly make an arrest or order an arrest within their local jurisdiction. [Source: Section 41, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest by Magistrate

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 41: Arrest by Magistrate

Q: A Judicial Magistrate is on vacation in another state and witnesses a crime. Can the Magistrate use their powers under this section to order an arrest?
A: No, under sub-section (1), the offence must be committed in the presence of a Magistrate "within his local jurisdiction." [Source: Section 41, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest by Magistrate

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 41: Arrest by Magistrate

Q: What conditions must be present for a Magistrate to arrest someone for a past crime?
A: Under sub-section (2), the Magistrate may arrest any person "within his local jurisdiction" for whose arrest "he is competent at the time and in the circumstances to issue a warrant." [Source: Section 41, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest by Magistrate

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 41: Arrest by Magistrate

Q: Does this section distinguish between the powers of an Executive Magistrate and a Judicial Magistrate?
A: No, the section grants these powers to "any Magistrate, whether Executive or Judicial." [Source: Section 41, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest by Magistrate

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 41: Arrest by Magistrate

Q: What is the immediate procedural consequence after a Magistrate arrests an offender who committed a crime in their presence?
A: Under sub-section (1), the Magistrate may thereupon, subject to the provisions contained regarding bail, "commit the offender to custody." [Source: Section 41, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest by Magistrate

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 42: Protection of members of the Armed Forces from arrest

Q: Can police freely arrest soldiers for actions taken during their military duties?
A: No member of the Armed Forces of the Union shall be arrested for anything done in the discharge of his official duties except with the consent of the Central Government. [Source: Section 42, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Protection of members of the Armed Forces from arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 42: Protection of members of the Armed Forces from arrest

Q: What does Section 42 of BNSS 2023 provide?
A: Section 42 of BNSS 2023 provides immunity from standard arrest procedures for members of the Armed Forces acting in the line of duty, requiring central or state government consent prior to arrest. [Source: Section 42, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Protection of members of the Armed Forces from arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 42: Protection of members of the Armed Forces from arrest

Q: The State Government wants to extend this arrest protection to a specific class of state police officers tasked with maintaining public order. Can they do this?
A: Yes, under sub-section (2), the State Government may by notification direct that the provisions shall apply to such class or category of members of the Forces charged with the maintenance of public order. [Source: Section 42, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Protection of members of the Armed Forces from arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 42: Protection of members of the Armed Forces from arrest

Q: What condition must a soldier's action meet to qualify for protection from arrest under this section?
A: The action must be something done or purported to be done "in the discharge of his official duties." [Source: Section 42, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Protection of members of the Armed Forces from arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 42: Protection of members of the Armed Forces from arrest

Q: Is this protection absolute, meaning a soldier can never be arrested for official acts?
A: No, under sub-section (1), they can be arrested, but only "with the consent of the Central Government." [Source: Section 42, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Protection of members of the Armed Forces from arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 42: Protection of members of the Armed Forces from arrest

Q: What is the consequence if a state uses sub-section (2) to extend protection to a class of state forces?
A: The consequence is that wherever the expression "Central Government" appears in the rule, it shall "be construed as a reference to the State Government" for those specific state forces. [Source: Section 42, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Protection of members of the Armed Forces from arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 43: Arrest how made

Q: How much physical force can police use when making an arrest?
A: The police officer may use all means necessary to effect the arrest if the person forcibly resists or attempts to evade, but does not have the right to cause the death of a person not accused of an offence punishable with death or life imprisonment. [Source: Section 43, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest how made

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 43: Arrest how made

Q: What is Section 43 of BNSS 2023 about?
A: Section 43 of BNSS 2023 outlines the physical procedure for making an arrest, including the rules on touching the suspect, using force, and the special procedures required when arresting women. [Source: Section 43, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest how made

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 43: Arrest how made

Q: A male police officer attempts to arrest a female suspect. The suspect refuses to submit to custody verbally. Can the male officer physically grab her to effect the arrest?
A: No, the proviso to sub-section (1) states that "no male police officer shall touch the person of a woman for making her arrest." [Source: Section 43, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest how made

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 43: Arrest how made

Q: Under what conditions is a police officer legally permitted to cause the death of a suspect while trying to arrest them?
A: Under sub-section (3), this is only permitted if the person is accused of "an offence punishable with death or with imprisonment for life." [Source: Section 43, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest how made

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 43: Arrest how made

Q: Are police allowed to arrest women after sunset and before sunrise?
A: Generally no, but under sub-section (4), in exceptional circumstances, a woman police officer may make the arrest after obtaining prior permission of the Judicial Magistrate of the first class. [Source: Section 43, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest how made

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 43: Arrest how made

Q: What happens if an arrested person submits to custody by word or action immediately upon encountering the police?
A: Under sub-section (1), the consequence is that the police officer making the arrest is not required to actually "touch or confine the body of the person to be arrested." [Source: Section 43, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest how made

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 44: Search of place entered by person sought to be arrested

Q: Can police enter a private house without a search warrant if they are chasing a suspect?
A: Yes, if a police officer has authority to arrest someone and believes the suspect has entered a place, the person in charge must allow them free ingress, and if denied, the officer may break open doors to enter and search. [Source: Section 44, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search of place entered by person sought to be arrested

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 44: Search of place entered by person sought to be arrested

Q: What does Section 44 of BNSS 2023 dictate?
A: Section 44 of BNSS 2023 dictates the rules for searching private places to find a person sought for arrest, including the authority to break open doors and the protocol for entering apartments occupied by women. [Source: Section 44, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search of place entered by person sought to be arrested

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 44: Search of place entered by person sought to be arrested

Q: A police officer chasing a suspect needs to break into an apartment. The apartment is occupied by a woman who, by custom, does not appear in public. Can the officer just break the door down immediately?
A: No, the proviso to sub-section (2) requires the officer to first "give notice to such female that she is at liberty to withdraw" and afford her every reasonable facility for withdrawing before entering. [Source: Section 44, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search of place entered by person sought to be arrested

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 44: Search of place entered by person sought to be arrested

Q: What conditions must an officer meet before breaking open an outer or inner door to gain admittance to a house?
A: Under sub-section (2), the officer must have a warrant or authority to arrest without opportunity of escape, must make a "notification of his authority and purpose," must make a "demand of admittance," and must be unable to otherwise obtain admittance. [Source: Section 44, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search of place entered by person sought to be arrested

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 44: Search of place entered by person sought to be arrested

Q: Is the power to break open doors only granted for the purpose of getting inside a house?
A: No, under sub-section (3), an officer may also break open doors or windows "in order to liberate himself or any other person who, having lawfully entered for the purpose of making an arrest, is detained therein." [Source: Section 44, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search of place entered by person sought to be arrested

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 44: Search of place entered by person sought to be arrested

Q: What is the legal duty of a homeowner when a police officer, acting under a warrant of arrest, demands to search their house for the suspect?
A: The consequence under sub-section (1) is that the homeowner "shall, on demand... allow him free ingress thereto, and afford all reasonable facilities for a search therein." [Source: Section 44, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search of place entered by person sought to be arrested

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 45: Pursuit of offenders into other jurisdictions

Q: Can a local police officer chase a suspect across state lines?
A: Yes, a police officer may, for the purpose of arresting without warrant any person whom he is authorised to arrest, pursue such person into any place in India. [Source: Section 45, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Pursuit of offenders into other jurisdictions

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 45: Pursuit of offenders into other jurisdictions

Q: What is Section 45 of BNSS 2023 about?
A: Section 45 of BNSS 2023 provides police officers with the nationwide geographical authority to pursue and arrest offenders they are otherwise legally authorized to arrest without a warrant. [Source: Section 45, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Pursuit of offenders into other jurisdictions

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 45: Pursuit of offenders into other jurisdictions

Q: An officer in Delhi sees a man commit a cognizable offence. The man immediately boards a train and flees. Can the Delhi officer chase him all the way to Mumbai and arrest him there?
A: Yes, under this section, the officer may "pursue such person into any place in India." [Source: Section 45, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Pursuit of offenders into other jurisdictions

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 45: Pursuit of offenders into other jurisdictions

Q: What condition must be met regarding the nature of the arrest for this cross-jurisdiction pursuit to be lawful?
A: The pursuit must be for the purpose of arresting "without warrant" any person "whom he is authorised to arrest." [Source: Section 45, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Pursuit of offenders into other jurisdictions

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 45: Pursuit of offenders into other jurisdictions

Q: Does this section give a police officer the power to conduct general investigations outside their jurisdiction?
A: No, it specifically authorizes them only to "pursue such person" for the purpose of "arresting without warrant." [Source: Section 45, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Pursuit of offenders into other jurisdictions

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 45: Pursuit of offenders into other jurisdictions

Q: What is the jurisdictional consequence of this section for a fleeing suspect?
A: The consequence is that crossing district or state borders within India does not legally invalidate a hot-pursuit arrest made by the pursuing officer. [Source: Section 45, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Pursuit of offenders into other jurisdictions

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 46: No unnecessary restraint

Q: Can police use handcuffs freely on every person they arrest?
A: The person arrested shall not be subjected to more restraint than is necessary to prevent his escape, and handcuffs can only be used under specific circumstances like if the person is a habitual offender or accused of a serious crime. [Source: Section 46, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: No unnecessary restraint

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 46: No unnecessary restraint

Q: What is Section 46 of BNSS 2023 about?
A: Section 46 of BNSS 2023 establishes that arrested persons should only face necessary restraint and outlines the specific conditions under which police officers are permitted to use handcuffs. [Source: Section 46, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: No unnecessary restraint

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 46: No unnecessary restraint

Q: An officer arrests a first-time offender for a minor theft. The suspect is completely cooperative. Can the officer handcuff them just to be safe?
A: No, the general rule is that "the person arrested shall not be subjected to more restraint than is necessary to prevent his escape," and minor theft by a first-time cooperative offender does not meet the criteria in sub-section (2). [Source: Section 46, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: No unnecessary restraint

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 46: No unnecessary restraint

Q: What conditions permit a police officer to use handcuffs on an arrested person?
A: Under sub-section (2), the officer may use handcuffs if the person is a habitual, repeat offender, has escaped custody before, has committed organized crime, terrorist acts, drug-related crimes, illegal possession of arms, murder, rape, acid attack, counterfeiting, human trafficking, sexual offences against children, or offences against the State. [Source: Section 46, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: No unnecessary restraint

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 46: No unnecessary restraint

Q: Is the use of handcuffs mandatory for all the serious offences listed in this section?
A: No, sub-section (2) states the police officer "may" use handcuffs, giving them discretion based on the nature and gravity of the offence. [Source: Section 46, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: No unnecessary restraint

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 46: No unnecessary restraint

Q: What is the consequence if a person is arrested for an offence against the State?
A: The consequence is that, considering the nature and gravity of the offence, the police officer is legally permitted under sub-section (2) to use handcuffs while making the arrest or producing them before court. [Source: Section 46, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: No unnecessary restraint

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 47: Person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest and of right to bail

Q: When police arrest someone without a warrant, what information must they provide to the suspect?
A: Every police officer or other person arresting any person without warrant shall forthwith communicate to him full particulars of the offence for which he is arrested or other grounds for such arrest. [Source: Section 47, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest and of right to bail

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 47: Person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest and of right to bail

Q: What does Section 47 of BNSS 2023 mandate?
A: Section 47 of BNSS 2023 mandates that anyone arresting a person without a warrant must immediately inform them of the grounds for arrest and, if applicable, their right to be released on bail. [Source: Section 47, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest and of right to bail

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 47: Person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest and of right to bail

Q: An officer arrests a suspect for a bailable offence without a warrant. The officer tells the suspect the charges but doesn't mention bail, hoping they'll stay in jail overnight. Is this legal?
A: No, under sub-section (2), if the offence is bailable, the officer "shall inform the person arrested that he is entitled to be released on bail and that he may arrange for sureties on his behalf." [Source: Section 47, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest and of right to bail

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 47: Person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest and of right to bail

Q: What condition requires an officer to inform an arrested person about arranging sureties?
A: This condition applies when a police officer arrests without warrant any person other than a person accused of a non-bailable offence. [Source: Section 47, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest and of right to bail

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 47: Person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest and of right to bail

Q: Does a private citizen who makes an arrest without a warrant have to inform the suspect of the grounds?
A: Yes, sub-section (1) applies to "Every police officer or other person" making an arrest without a warrant. [Source: Section 47, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest and of right to bail

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 47: Person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest and of right to bail

Q: What is the procedural consequence of arresting someone for a bailable offence without a warrant?
A: The consequence, under sub-section (2), is the immediate legal obligation for the arresting officer to inform the arrested person of their entitlement to bail. [Source: Section 47, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest and of right to bail

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 48: Obligation of person making arrest to inform about the arrest, etc., to a nominated person

Q: Who gets to know when someone is arrested?
A: Every police officer or other person making any arrest under this Sanhita must immediately give information regarding the arrest and the place of detainment to any of the arrested person's friends, relatives, or other persons nominated by them. [Source: Section 48, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Obligation of person making arrest to inform about the arrest, etc., to a nominated person

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 48: Obligation of person making arrest to inform about the arrest, etc., to a nominated person

Q: What is Section 48 of BNSS 2023 about?
A: Section 48 of BNSS 2023 establishes the obligation of arresting officers to inform a person nominated by the arrestee about the arrest, the right to nominate someone, and the documentation of this process. [Source: Section 48, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Obligation of person making arrest to inform about the arrest, etc., to a nominated person

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 48: Obligation of person making arrest to inform about the arrest, etc., to a nominated person

Q: An officer arrests someone and immediately locks them up without telling them they can call a friend. When the suspect's family finds out two days later, they complain. Did the officer violate the Act?
A: Yes, under sub-section (2), the police officer "shall inform the arrested person of his rights under sub-section (1) as soon as he is brought to the police station." [Source: Section 48, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Obligation of person making arrest to inform about the arrest, etc., to a nominated person

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 48: Obligation of person making arrest to inform about the arrest, etc., to a nominated person

Q: What specific details must be recorded in the police station's book regarding this notification?
A: Under sub-section (3), an entry of the fact as to who has been informed of the arrest must be made in a book kept in the police station. [Source: Section 48, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Obligation of person making arrest to inform about the arrest, etc., to a nominated person

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 48: Obligation of person making arrest to inform about the arrest, etc., to a nominated person

Q: Is it solely the police officer's choice who gets notified about an arrest?
A: No, under sub-section (1), the information is given to friends, relatives, or "such other persons as may be disclosed or nominated by the arrested person." [Source: Section 48, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Obligation of person making arrest to inform about the arrest, etc., to a nominated person

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 48: Obligation of person making arrest to inform about the arrest, etc., to a nominated person

Q: What is the Magistrate's duty when an arrested person is brought before them?
A: The consequence is that, under sub-section (4), the Magistrate is legally obligated to "satisfy himself that the requirements of sub-section (2) and sub-section (3) have been complied with" regarding informing the nominated person. [Source: Section 48, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Obligation of person making arrest to inform about the arrest, etc., to a nominated person

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 49: Search of arrested person

Q: Can police search the pockets and belongings of a person they just arrested?
A: Yes, whenever a person is arrested and not released on bail, the officer making the arrest may search such person and place all articles found, other than necessary wearing-apparel, in safe custody. [Source: Section 49, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search of arrested person

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 49: Search of arrested person

Q: What does Section 49 of BNSS 2023 cover?
A: Section 49 of BNSS 2023 covers the protocol for searching arrested individuals who are not granted bail, the handling of seized items, and the specific requirement for searching women. [Source: Section 49, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search of arrested person

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 49: Search of arrested person

Q: A male police officer arrests a woman and decides to search her for hidden weapons. Is this procedure lawful?
A: No, under sub-section (2), whenever it is necessary to cause a female to be searched, "the search shall be made by another female with strict regard to decency." [Source: Section 49, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search of arrested person

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 49: Search of arrested person

Q: What conditions must be met before an officer can legally search an arrested person under this section?
A: The person must be arrested by a police officer under a warrant that doesn't provide for bail (or they can't furnish it), or arrested without a warrant/by a private person and cannot legally be admitted to bail or is unable to furnish bail. [Source: Section 49, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search of arrested person

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 49: Search of arrested person

Q: Can the police confiscate a person's necessary clothing during a search?
A: No, under sub-section (1), they must place all articles in safe custody "other than necessary wearing-apparel." [Source: Section 49, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search of arrested person

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 49: Search of arrested person

Q: What is the documentary consequence when an officer seizes an item from an arrested person during a search?
A: The consequence is that, under sub-section (1), "a receipt showing the articles taken in possession by the police officer shall be given to such person." [Source: Section 49, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search of arrested person

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 50: Power to seize offensive weapons

Q: What happens if an arrested person is carrying a dangerous weapon?
A: The officer or other person making any arrest under this Sanhita may take from the person arrested any offensive weapons which he has about his person. [Source: Section 50, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to seize offensive weapons

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 50: Power to seize offensive weapons

Q: What is Section 50 of BNSS 2023 about?
A: Section 50 of BNSS 2023 grants arresting officers and private individuals the power to seize offensive weapons from an arrested person and dictates that those weapons must be delivered to the court or officer. [Source: Section 50, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to seize offensive weapons

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 50: Power to seize offensive weapons

Q: A private citizen makes a lawful arrest under Section 40 and disarms the suspect of a knife. The citizen decides to keep the knife. Is this lawful?
A: No, the citizen "shall deliver all weapons so taken to the Court or officer before which or whom the officer or person making the arrest is required by this Sanhita to produce the person arrested." [Source: Section 50, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to seize offensive weapons

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 50: Power to seize offensive weapons

Q: Under what condition is the seizure of weapons authorized under this section?
A: The seizure is authorized when an officer or other person is "making any arrest under this Sanhita" and the arrested person has offensive weapons "about his person." [Source: Section 50, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to seize offensive weapons

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 50: Power to seize offensive weapons

Q: Does this section only apply to police officers making an arrest?
A: No, it applies to "The officer or other person making any arrest," which includes private citizens authorized to arrest under the Sanhita. [Source: Section 50, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to seize offensive weapons

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 50: Power to seize offensive weapons

Q: What is the procedural consequence after an arresting officer seizes an offensive weapon from a suspect?
A: The consequence is that the officer is legally required to deliver that seized weapon to the Court or officer where the arrested person is produced. [Source: Section 50, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to seize offensive weapons

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 51: Examination of accused by medical practitioner at the request of police officer

Q: Can the police force an arrested suspect to undergo a medical or DNA examination to gather evidence?
A: Yes, if there are reasonable grounds to believe an examination will afford evidence as to the commission of an offence, a registered medical practitioner may examine the arrested person at the request of a police officer not below the rank of Sub-Inspector. [Source: Section 51, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Examination of accused by medical practitioner at the request of police officer

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 51: Examination of accused by medical practitioner at the request of police officer

Q: What does Section 51 of BNSS 2023 dictate?
A: Section 51 of BNSS 2023 allows police officers to request medical and DNA examinations of arrested persons if it will yield evidence, and outlines the use of reasonable force and procedures for examining women. [Source: Section 51, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Examination of accused by medical practitioner at the request of police officer

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 51: Examination of accused by medical practitioner at the request of police officer

Q: An arrested suspect violently refuses to let a doctor draw blood or take swabs. Can the doctor and police use physical force to conduct the examination?
A: Yes, under sub-section (1), it shall be lawful for the medical practitioner and those acting in good faith in his aid to use "such force as is reasonably necessary for that purpose." [Source: Section 51, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Examination of accused by medical practitioner at the request of police officer

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 51: Examination of accused by medical practitioner at the request of police officer

Q: What conditions are required for a police officer to legally request this medical examination?
A: The person must be arrested on a charge of committing an offence of such a nature and under such circumstances that there are "reasonable grounds for believing that an examination of his person will afford evidence," and the requesting officer must not be below the rank of Sub-Inspector. [Source: Section 51, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Examination of accused by medical practitioner at the request of police officer

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 51: Examination of accused by medical practitioner at the request of police officer

Q: Can any doctor perform this examination on a female suspect?
A: No, under sub-section (2), the examination of a female shall be made "only by, or under the supervision of, a female registered medical practitioner." [Source: Section 51, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Examination of accused by medical practitioner at the request of police officer

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 51: Examination of accused by medical practitioner at the request of police officer

Q: What is the consequence if the medical practitioner completes an examination under this section?
A: The consequence, under sub-section (3), is that the practitioner must, without delay, forward the examination report to the investigating officer. [Source: Section 51, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Examination of accused by medical practitioner at the request of police officer

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 52: Examination of person accused of rape by medical practitioner

Q: How is medical evidence gathered from a person arrested for rape?
A: When a person is arrested for rape or an attempt to commit rape, a registered medical practitioner employed in a hospital may examine their person to gather evidence, upon the request of a police officer not below the rank of Sub-Inspector. [Source: Section 52, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Examination of person accused of rape by medical practitioner

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 52: Examination of person accused of rape by medical practitioner

Q: What does Section 52 of BNSS 2023 cover?
A: Section 52 of BNSS 2023 details the mandatory medical examination procedure for a person accused of rape, the contents required in the medical report, and the timeline for forwarding the report. [Source: Section 52, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Examination of person accused of rape by medical practitioner

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 52: Examination of person accused of rape by medical practitioner

Q: A doctor examines a rape suspect but forgets to record the exact time the examination started and ended in the report. Is the report legally complete?
A: No, under clause (d) of sub-section (2), the report must specifically record "the exact time of commencement and completion of the examination." [Source: Section 52, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Examination of person accused of rape by medical practitioner

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 52: Examination of person accused of rape by medical practitioner

Q: What condition applies if a government hospital doctor is not available within a sixteen-kilometer radius of the incident?
A: Under sub-section (1), if a medical practitioner employed in a hospital run by the Government or local authority is not available, the examination may be conducted by "any other registered medical practitioner." [Source: Section 52, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Examination of person accused of rape by medical practitioner

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 52: Examination of person accused of rape by medical practitioner

Q: Is it enough for the medical report to just list the physical injuries observed on the accused?
A: No, under sub-section (3), the report must explicitly state "precisely the reasons for each conclusion arrived at." [Source: Section 52, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Examination of person accused of rape by medical practitioner

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 52: Examination of person accused of rape by medical practitioner

Q: What is the procedural consequence once the medical practitioner finishes writing the examination report?
A: The consequence, under sub-section (4), is that the practitioner must, without delay, forward the report to the investigating officer, who shall then forward it to the Magistrate. [Source: Section 52, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Examination of person accused of rape by medical practitioner

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 53: Examination of arrested person by medical officer

Q: Is every arrested person required to have a medical checkup?
A: Every person who is arrested shall be examined by a medical officer in the service of Central Government or State Government, or by a registered medical practitioner, soon after the arrest is made. [Source: Section 53, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Examination of arrested person by medical officer

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 53: Examination of arrested person by medical officer

Q: What is Section 53 of BNSS 2023 about?
A: Section 53 of BNSS 2023 mandates a general medical examination for every arrested person immediately after arrest to document injuries and general health, with specific provisions for examining women. [Source: Section 53, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Examination of arrested person by medical officer

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 53: Examination of arrested person by medical officer

Q: A female suspect is arrested and needs her mandatory medical examination. A male government doctor is the only one on duty. Can he perform the examination?
A: No, under the proviso to sub-section (1), where the arrested person is a female, the examination of the body shall be made "only by or under the supervision of a female medical officer, and in case the female medical officer is not available, by a female registered medical practitioner." [Source: Section 53, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Examination of arrested person by medical officer

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 53: Examination of arrested person by medical officer

Q: What specific details must the medical officer include in the record of the examination?
A: Under sub-section (2), the officer shall prepare a record of the examination, mentioning therein "any injuries or marks of violence upon the person arrested, and the approximate time when such injuries or marks may have been inflicted." [Source: Section 53, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Examination of arrested person by medical officer

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 53: Examination of arrested person by medical officer

Q: Does this examination only apply to suspects who are physically injured during the arrest?
A: No, sub-section (1) applies to "Every person who is arrested," making the examination a universal requirement regardless of visible injury. [Source: Section 53, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Examination of arrested person by medical officer

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 53: Examination of arrested person by medical officer

Q: What is the documentary consequence once the medical examination of the arrested person is complete?
A: The consequence, under sub-section (3), is that a copy of the medical report must be furnished to the arrested person or the person nominated by them under sub-section (2) of section 48. [Source: Section 53, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Examination of arrested person by medical officer

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 54: Identification of person arrested

Q: Can a court force an arrested person to be put in an identification lineup?
A: Yes, where a person is arrested and his identification by any other person is considered necessary for investigation, the Court having jurisdiction may, on the request of the officer in charge of a police station, direct the person to subject himself to identification. [Source: Section 54, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Identification of person arrested

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 54: Identification of person arrested

Q: What is the purpose of Section 54 of BNSS 2023?
A: Section 54 of BNSS 2023 allows courts to order arrested individuals to participate in identification processes, and mandates special accommodations and video recording if the identifier is disabled. [Source: Section 54, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Identification of person arrested

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 54: Identification of person arrested

Q: A blind witness needs to identify a suspect. Can the police just conduct a normal voice lineup on their own?
A: No, if the identifying person is physically disabled, the process shall take place "under the supervision of a Magistrate who shall take appropriate steps to ensure that such person identifies the person arrested using methods that person is comfortable with." [Source: Section 54, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Identification of person arrested

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 54: Identification of person arrested

Q: Who must request the identification process before the court can direct the arrested person to comply?
A: The Court may direct this "on the request of the officer in charge of a police station." [Source: Section 54, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Identification of person arrested

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 54: Identification of person arrested

Q: Is an audio-video recording of the identification process always mandatory for every lineup?
A: The section explicitly mandates that "the identification process shall be recorded by any audio-video electronic means" specifically when the person identifying the arrested person is mentally or physically disabled. [Source: Section 54, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Identification of person arrested

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 54: Identification of person arrested

Q: What is the consequence of a court issuing a direction under this section?
A: The consequence is that the arrested person is legally compelled to "subject himself to identification by any person or persons in such manner as the Court may deem fit." [Source: Section 54, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Identification of person arrested

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 55: Procedure when police officer deputes subordinate to arrest without warrant

Q: Can a senior police officer just verbally tell a subordinate to go arrest someone without a warrant?
A: No, the officer must deliver to the subordinate "an order in writing, specifying the person to be arrested and the offence or other cause for which the arrest is to be made." [Source: Section 55, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Procedure when police officer deputes subordinate to arrest without warrant

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 55: Procedure when police officer deputes subordinate to arrest without warrant

Q: What procedure does Section 55 of BNSS 2023 establish?
A: Section 55 of BNSS 2023 establishes the requirement for written orders and notification of substance when a police officer in charge of a station deputes a subordinate to arrest someone without a warrant. [Source: Section 55, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Procedure when police officer deputes subordinate to arrest without warrant

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 55: Procedure when police officer deputes subordinate to arrest without warrant
