A: The consequence is that it prevents officers from dragging suspects on long journeys across the country without first allowing a local, neutral magistrate to verify the arrest and consider bail. [Source: Section 82, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Procedure on arrest of person against whom warrant issued

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 83: Procedure by Magistrate before whom such person arrested is brought

Q: What happens when an out-of-district arrestee is brought before the local Magistrate?
A: The Magistrate will verify the person's identity and direct their removal to the issuing Court, unless the offence is bailable or they are granted bail by the local higher courts. [Source: Section 83, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Procedure by Magistrate before whom such person arrested is brought

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 83: Procedure by Magistrate before whom such person arrested is brought

Q: What is Section 83 of BNSS 2023 about?
A: Section 83 of BNSS 2023 outlines the process for a local Magistrate to handle a suspect arrested on an out-of-district warrant, including verifying identity, arranging transit, and evaluating bail. [Source: Section 83, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Procedure by Magistrate before whom such person arrested is brought

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 83: Procedure by Magistrate before whom such person arrested is brought

Q: An individual is arrested on an out-of-district warrant for a non-bailable offence. They are brought before the local Executive Magistrate and ask for bail. Can the Executive Magistrate grant it?
A: No, the second proviso states that if the offence is non-bailable, it shall be lawful only for the "Chief Judicial Magistrate... or the Sessions Judge" of that local district to release such person on bail. [Source: Section 83, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Procedure by Magistrate before whom such person arrested is brought

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 83: Procedure by Magistrate before whom such person arrested is brought

Q: What is the primary condition the Magistrate must verify before directing the person's removal to the originating Court?
A: They must verify "if the person arrested appears to be the person intended by the Court which issued the warrant." [Source: Section 83, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Procedure by Magistrate before whom such person arrested is brought

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 83: Procedure by Magistrate before whom such person arrested is brought

Q: Does presenting the arrested person to the Magistrate nullify a police officer's power to release them on a bailable warrant?
A: No, sub-section (2) states "Nothing in this section shall be deemed to prevent a police officer from taking security under section 73." [Source: Section 83, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Procedure by Magistrate before whom such person arrested is brought

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 83: Procedure by Magistrate before whom such person arrested is brought

Q: What is the consequence if the arrested person is willing and able to provide the required bail bond for a bailable offence?
A: The consequence is that the local Magistrate "shall take such bail bond or security... and forward the bond, to the Court which issued the warrant," effectively releasing the person from immediate physical transit. [Source: Section 83, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Procedure by Magistrate before whom such person arrested is brought

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 84: Proclamation for person absconding

Q: What can a court do if a suspect hides to avoid an arrest warrant?
A: The Court may publish a written proclamation requiring the person to appear at a specified place and time, not less than thirty days from the publication date. [Source: Section 84, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proclamation for person absconding

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 84: Proclamation for person absconding

Q: What does Section 84 of BNSS 2023 establish?
A: Section 84 of BNSS 2023 establishes the procedure for publicly proclaiming a person as absconding, detailing the methods of publication and the process to officially declare them a "proclaimed offender." [Source: Section 84, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proclamation for person absconding

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 84: Proclamation for person absconding

Q: A judge publishes a proclamation on June 1st, demanding an absconding suspect appear in court on June 15th. Is this timeline valid?
A: No, sub-section (1) requires the specified time to be "not less than thirty days from the date of publishing such proclamation." [Source: Section 84, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proclamation for person absconding

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 84: Proclamation for person absconding

Q: What are the three mandatory physical locations where the proclamation must be published under sub-section (2)(i)?
A: It must be (a) publicly read in a conspicuous place in their town/village, (b) affixed to their house/homestead or a conspicuous place in the town, and (c) affixed to a conspicuous part of the Court-house. [Source: Section 84, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proclamation for person absconding

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 84: Proclamation for person absconding

Q: Can the court declare absolutely anyone who fails to appear a "proclaimed offender"?
A: No, under sub-section (4), this specific declaration is only for a person accused of an offence "punishable with imprisonment of ten years or more, or imprisonment for life or with death." [Source: Section 84, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proclamation for person absconding

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 84: Proclamation for person absconding

Q: What is the evidentiary consequence of the Court issuing a written statement that the proclamation was duly published?
A: Under sub-section (3), such a statement "shall be conclusive evidence that the requirements of this section have been complied with." [Source: Section 84, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proclamation for person absconding

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 85: Attachment of property of person absconding

Q: Can the government seize the property of someone who runs away from a warrant?
A: Yes, a Court issuing a proclamation for an absconding person may order the attachment of any of their movable or immovable property. [Source: Section 85, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Attachment of property of person absconding

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 85: Attachment of property of person absconding

Q: What does Section 85 of BNSS 2023 detail?
A: Section 85 of BNSS 2023 details the court's power to attach the property of an absconding person, outlining the different methods for attaching debts, movable goods, and immovable land. [Source: Section 85, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Attachment of property of person absconding

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 85: Attachment of property of person absconding

Q: A court learns an absconding suspect is actively trying to sell their house before fleeing the state entirely. Can the court attach the property immediately upon issuing the proclamation?
A: Yes, under the proviso to sub-section (1), if the court is satisfied the person "is about to dispose of the whole or any part of his property," it may "order the attachment of property simultaneously with the issue of the proclamation." [Source: Section 85, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Attachment of property of person absconding

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 85: Attachment of property of person absconding

Q: What are three methods mentioned in sub-section (3) for attaching a debt or movable property?
A: The attachment can be made "(a) by seizure; or (b) by the appointment of a receiver; or (c) by an order in writing prohibiting the delivery of such property." [Source: Section 85, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Attachment of property of person absconding

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 85: Attachment of property of person absconding

Q: Does attached property just sit idle until the suspect is caught?
A: Not always; under sub-section (5), if the property consists of "live-stock or is of a perishable nature," the Court may order its "immediate sale." [Source: Section 85, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Attachment of property of person absconding

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 85: Attachment of property of person absconding

Q: What is the consequence of attaching land that pays revenue to the State Government?
A: The consequence, under sub-section (4), is that the attachment must be made specifically "through the Collector of the district in which the land is situate." [Source: Section 85, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Attachment of property of person absconding

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 86: Identification and attachment of property of proclaimed person

Q: How can authorities target the property of a proclaimed offender who has hidden assets?
A: The Court may, on the written request of a high-ranking police officer, initiate the process of requesting assistance from a Court or authority in a contracting State to identify, attach, and forfeit the property. [Source: Section 86, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Identification and attachment of property of proclaimed person

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 86: Identification and attachment of property of proclaimed person

Q: What is the purpose of Section 86 of BNSS 2023?
A: Section 86 of BNSS 2023 empowers courts to seek international assistance from contracting States to trace and attach the property of a proclaimed person. [Source: Section 86, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Identification and attachment of property of proclaimed person

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 86: Identification and attachment of property of proclaimed person

Q: A local Sub-Inspector discovers a proclaimed offender has money in a foreign bank. The Sub-Inspector directly asks the Court to initiate international attachment. Can the court proceed on this request?
A: No, the written request must come from "a police officer not below the rank of the Superintendent of Police or Commissioner of Police." [Source: Section 86, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Identification and attachment of property of proclaimed person

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 86: Identification and attachment of property of proclaimed person

Q: What specific actions can be requested from the contracting State under this section?
A: Assistance can be requested for "identification, attachment and forfeiture of property belonging to a proclaimed person." [Source: Section 86, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Identification and attachment of property of proclaimed person

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 86: Identification and attachment of property of proclaimed person

Q: Can this section be used to attach property located entirely within the domestic district of the issuing Court?
A: No, this specific section is explicitly for "requesting assistance from a Court or an authority in the contracting State" which involves international or cross-jurisdictional treaties governed by Chapter VIII. [Source: Section 86, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Identification and attachment of property of proclaimed person

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 86: Identification and attachment of property of proclaimed person

Q: What is the procedural consequence once the Court initiates this process?
A: The consequence is that the identification and attachment must proceed "in accordance with the procedure provided in Chapter VIII." [Source: Section 86, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Identification and attachment of property of proclaimed person

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 87: Claims and objections to attachment

Q: What happens if the court accidentally attaches property that actually belongs to an innocent third party?
A: Any person other than the proclaimed person who has an interest in the property can file a claim or objection within six months of the attachment, and the Court shall inquire into it. [Source: Section 87, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Claims and objections to attachment

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 87: Claims and objections to attachment

Q: What does Section 87 of BNSS 2023 state?
A: Section 87 of BNSS 2023 states the procedure and timeline for third parties to contest the attachment of property, and allows them to file a civil suit if their claim is rejected by the Magistrate. [Source: Section 87, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Claims and objections to attachment

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 87: Claims and objections to attachment

Q: A woman claims the car attached by the court actually belongs to her, not the absconding suspect. She files an objection one year after the attachment. Will the court inquire into it?
A: No, under sub-section (1), the claim or objection must be made "within six months from the date of such attachment." [Source: Section 87, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Claims and objections to attachment

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 87: Claims and objections to attachment

Q: What two things must a third party establish in their objection under sub-section (1)?
A: They must establish that the claimant "has an interest in such property" and that "such interest is not liable to attachment under section 85." [Source: Section 87, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Claims and objections to attachment

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 87: Claims and objections to attachment

Q: If the person who filed the objection dies before the court makes a decision, is the claim automatically dropped?
A: No, the proviso to sub-section (1) states that in the event of death, the claim "may be continued by his legal representative." [Source: Section 87, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Claims and objections to attachment

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 87: Claims and objections to attachment

Q: What is the consequence if the Magistrate completely disallows a third party's valid claim?
A: The consequence, under sub-section (4), is that the aggrieved person may "within a period of one year from the date of such order, institute a suit to establish the right which he claims" in a civil court. [Source: Section 87, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Claims and objections to attachment

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 88: Release, sale and restoration of attached property

Q: What happens to the attached property if the absconding person eventually surrenders to the court?
A: If the proclaimed person appears within the time specified in the proclamation, the Court shall make an order releasing the property from attachment. [Source: Section 88, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Release, sale and restoration of attached property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 88: Release, sale and restoration of attached property

Q: What does Section 88 of BNSS 2023 outline?
A: Section 88 of BNSS 2023 outlines the rules governing what happens to attached property, detailing when it can be released, sold, or restored to a proclaimed person who later appears and proves they did not intentionally abscond. [Source: Section 88, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Release, sale and restoration of attached property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 88: Release, sale and restoration of attached property

Q: A proclaimed person fails to appear. Three months later, the State Government immediately tries to sell their attached house. Is this sale legally permitted at this time?
A: No, under sub-section (2), the property "shall not be sold until the expiration of six months from the date of the attachment" and until any claims have been disposed of, unless it is subject to speedy decay. [Source: Section 88, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Release, sale and restoration of attached property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 88: Release, sale and restoration of attached property

Q: What two things must a proclaimed person prove to get their property or its proceeds back if they appear within two years?
A: They must prove "that he did not abscond or conceal himself for the purpose of avoiding execution of the warrant" and "that he had not such notice of the proclamation as to enable him to attend within the time specified therein." [Source: Section 88, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Release, sale and restoration of attached property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 88: Release, sale and restoration of attached property

Q: Does the six-month waiting period for selling attached property apply to everything?
A: No, an exception exists if the property "is subject to speedy and natural decay, or the Court considers that the sale would be for the benefit of the owner." [Source: Section 88, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Release, sale and restoration of attached property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 88: Release, sale and restoration of attached property

Q: What is the financial consequence if the State Government sells the property and the owner later successfully proves they didn't intentionally abscond?
A: The consequence is that the "net proceeds of the sale... shall, after satisfying therefrom all costs incurred in consequence of the attachment, be delivered to him." [Source: Section 88, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Release, sale and restoration of attached property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 89: Appeal from order rejecting application for restoration of attached property

Q: What can a person do if a judge refuses to return their attached property after they prove they weren't hiding?
A: Any person aggrieved by a refusal to deliver property or the proceeds of its sale may appeal to the Court to which appeals ordinarily lie from the sentences of that initial Court. [Source: Section 89, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Appeal from order rejecting application for restoration of attached property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 89: Appeal from order rejecting application for restoration of attached property

Q: What does Section 89 of BNSS 2023 provide?
A: Section 89 of BNSS 2023 provides an explicit appellate remedy for individuals whose application to restore their attached property under section 88 has been wrongfully denied by the lower court. [Source: Section 89, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Appeal from order rejecting application for restoration of attached property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 89: Appeal from order rejecting application for restoration of attached property

Q: A proclaimed person reappears, proves they never saw the proclamation, but the Magistrate arbitrarily refuses to return the sale proceeds of their house. Which court should they go to next?
A: They must appeal to "the Court to which appeals ordinarily lie from the sentences of the first-mentioned Court." [Source: Section 89, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Appeal from order rejecting application for restoration of attached property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 89: Appeal from order rejecting application for restoration of attached property

Q: Who specifically is granted the right to appeal under this section?
A: The right is granted to "Any person referred to in sub-section (3) of section 88, who is aggrieved by any refusal to deliver property or the proceeds of the sale thereof." [Source: Section 89, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Appeal from order rejecting application for restoration of attached property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 89: Appeal from order rejecting application for restoration of attached property

Q: Does this section allow third parties to appeal if their claims under Section 87 were rejected?
A: No, this section explicitly limits the appeal to "Any person referred to in sub-section (3) of section 88," which pertains only to the proclaimed person, not third-party claimants. [Source: Section 89, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Appeal from order rejecting application for restoration of attached property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 89: Appeal from order rejecting application for restoration of attached property

Q: What is the consequence of this section regarding the Magistrate's power?
A: The consequence is that the Magistrate's decision to retain the property or proceeds is not final and absolute, but is subject to oversight and reversal by a higher appellate court. [Source: Section 89, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Appeal from order rejecting application for restoration of attached property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 90: Issue of warrant in lieu of, or in addition to, summons

Q: Can a court just skip sending a summons and immediately issue an arrest warrant?
A: Yes, a Court empowered to issue a summons may, after recording its reasons in writing, issue a warrant for a person's arrest if it believes they have absconded or will not obey the summons. [Source: Section 90, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Issue of warrant in lieu of, or in addition to, summons

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 90: Issue of warrant in lieu of, or in addition to, summons

Q: What is Section 90 of BNSS 2023 about?
A: Section 90 of BNSS 2023 gives courts the discretion to elevate the level of compulsion, allowing them to issue an arrest warrant instead of or alongside a summons if they suspect evasion or non-compliance. [Source: Section 90, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Issue of warrant in lieu of, or in addition to, summons

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 90: Issue of warrant in lieu of, or in addition to, summons

Q: A judge realizes a witness they summoned yesterday is actively packing their bags to flee the country to avoid testifying. Can the judge issue an arrest warrant today before the hearing?
A: Yes, under clause (a), if the Court sees reason to believe "he has absconded or will not obey the summons," it may issue a warrant either before or after the issue of the summons. [Source: Section 90, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Issue of warrant in lieu of, or in addition to, summons

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 90: Issue of warrant in lieu of, or in addition to, summons

Q: What procedural step must the Court take before exercising this power to issue a warrant?
A: The Court must issue the warrant "after recording its reasons in writing." [Source: Section 90, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Issue of warrant in lieu of, or in addition to, summons

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 90: Issue of warrant in lieu of, or in addition to, summons

Q: Does a court need proof of absconding if the person simply missed their court date?
A: No, under clause (b), a warrant can be issued if they fail to appear, the summons is "proved to have been duly served in time," and "no reasonable excuse is offered for such failure." [Source: Section 90, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Issue of warrant in lieu of, or in addition to, summons

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 90: Issue of warrant in lieu of, or in addition to, summons

Q: What is the consequence of a person ignoring a properly served summons without a valid excuse?
A: The consequence is that the Court can immediately escalate the situation by issuing a warrant for their arrest, actively depriving them of their liberty to compel attendance. [Source: Section 90, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Issue of warrant in lieu of, or in addition to, summons

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 91: Power to take bond or bail bond for appearance

Q: If someone the court wants to summon happens to already be sitting in the courtroom, what can the judge do?
A: The presiding officer may require such person to execute a bond or bail bond for his appearance in that Court, or any other Court to which the case may be transferred. [Source: Section 91, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to take bond or bail bond for appearance

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 91: Power to take bond or bail bond for appearance

Q: What does Section 91 of BNSS 2023 state?
A: Section 91 of BNSS 2023 states that if a person who could be summoned or arrested is already physically present in the court, the officer presiding can immediately compel them to sign a bond ensuring future appearance. [Source: Section 91, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to take bond or bail bond for appearance

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 91: Power to take bond or bail bond for appearance

Q: A witness is in court watching a different trial. The judge recognizes him as someone needed for tomorrow's case. Instead of issuing a summons for tomorrow, the judge demands he sign a bail bond right then and there. Is this legal?
A: Yes, because the person "is present in such Court," the officer presiding may require him to execute a bond or bail bond for his appearance. [Source: Section 91, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to take bond or bail bond for appearance

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 91: Power to take bond or bail bond for appearance

Q: What condition regarding the presiding officer's authority is required to use this power?
A: The presiding officer must be "empowered to issue a summons or warrant" for that person's appearance or arrest. [Source: Section 91, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to take bond or bail bond for appearance

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 91: Power to take bond or bail bond for appearance

Q: Does this bond only guarantee appearance in that specific physical courtroom?
A: No, it guarantees appearance in "such Court, or any other Court to which the case may be transferred for trial." [Source: Section 91, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to take bond or bail bond for appearance

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 91: Power to take bond or bail bond for appearance

Q: What is the practical consequence of this section for court efficiency?
A: The consequence is that the court saves time and resources by immediately securing a guarantee of future attendance without having to initiate the formal process of dispatching a summons or warrant. [Source: Section 91, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to take bond or bail bond for appearance

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 92: Arrest on breach of bond or bail bond for appearance

Q: What happens if someone signs a bond promising to show up in court but then doesn't?
A: When a person bound by a bond or bail bond does not appear, the officer presiding in such Court may issue a warrant directing that they be arrested and produced before him. [Source: Section 92, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest on breach of bond or bail bond for appearance

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 92: Arrest on breach of bond or bail bond for appearance

Q: What does Section 92 of BNSS 2023 outline?
A: Section 92 of BNSS 2023 outlines the immediate enforcement mechanism—the issuance of an arrest warrant—when an individual violates the terms of their bond or bail bond by failing to appear in court. [Source: Section 92, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest on breach of bond or bail bond for appearance

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 92: Arrest on breach of bond or bail bond for appearance

Q: A person signs a bail bond and skips their trial date. Can the judge issue an arrest warrant, or must they only penalize the financial sureties?
A: The judge can issue a warrant; the section states the presiding officer "may issue a warrant directing that such person be arrested." [Source: Section 92, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest on breach of bond or bail bond for appearance

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 92: Arrest on breach of bond or bail bond for appearance

Q: What triggers the court's power to issue an arrest warrant under this specific section?
A: The trigger is when any person who is "bound by any bond or bail bond taken under this Sanhita to appear before a Court, does not appear." [Source: Section 92, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest on breach of bond or bail bond for appearance

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 92: Arrest on breach of bond or bail bond for appearance

Q: Is the presiding officer legally forced to issue a warrant the moment the person doesn't show up?
A: The language says the officer "may issue a warrant," implying they have the discretion to do so or to consider valid excuses before taking action. [Source: Section 92, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest on breach of bond or bail bond for appearance

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 92: Arrest on breach of bond or bail bond for appearance

Q: What is the punitive consequence for an individual who breaches their appearance bond?
A: The consequence is the immediate loss of their freedom; the court converts their failure to appear into an active order for their physical arrest and forced production in court. [Source: Section 92, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Arrest on breach of bond or bail bond for appearance

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 93: Provisions of this Chapter generally applicable to summons and warrants of arrest

Q: Do the rules for serving a summons apply to all types of summons issued under this Sanhita?
A: Yes, the provisions in this Chapter relating to summons and warrants, their issue, service, and execution, apply generally to every summons and every warrant of arrest issued under the Sanhita. [Source: Section 93, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Provisions of this Chapter generally applicable to summons and warrants of arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 93: Provisions of this Chapter generally applicable to summons and warrants of arrest

Q: What is the purpose of Section 93 of BNSS 2023?
A: Section 93 of BNSS 2023 acts as a unifying clause, extending the specific rules governing the service and execution of summons and warrants found in this Chapter to any such process issued anywhere in the Sanhita. [Source: Section 93, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Provisions of this Chapter generally applicable to summons and warrants of arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 93: Provisions of this Chapter generally applicable to summons and warrants of arrest

Q: A judge issues a specialized summons under a completely different chapter of the BNSS. Do the rules for "service when persons cannot be found" from this chapter still apply?
A: Yes, because the provisions of this Chapter "shall, so far as may be, apply to every summons and every warrant of arrest issued under this Sanhita." [Source: Section 93, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Provisions of this Chapter generally applicable to summons and warrants of arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 93: Provisions of this Chapter generally applicable to summons and warrants of arrest

Q: What specific aspects of summons and warrants are universally governed by this chapter's provisions?
A: The provisions relating to "their issue, service and execution" are the aspects made universally applicable. [Source: Section 93, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Provisions of this Chapter generally applicable to summons and warrants of arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 93: Provisions of this Chapter generally applicable to summons and warrants of arrest

Q: Do these rules apply with absolute rigidity to every single warrant regardless of context?
A: No, the phrase "so far as may be" provides a degree of flexibility, allowing the rules to apply generally but permitting reasonable deviation if the context of another section demands it. [Source: Section 93, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Provisions of this Chapter generally applicable to summons and warrants of arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 93: Provisions of this Chapter generally applicable to summons and warrants of arrest

Q: What is the structural consequence of this section within the Sanhita?
A: The consequence is that it prevents redundant drafting; the code does not need to redefine how to serve a summons or execute a warrant in every subsequent chapter where such powers are granted. [Source: Section 93, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Provisions of this Chapter generally applicable to summons and warrants of arrest

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 94: Summons to produce document or other thing

Q: Can police force someone to hand over their laptop or phone for an investigation?
A: Yes, any Court or officer in charge of a police station can issue a written order or summons requiring a person to produce a document, electronic communication, or communication device necessary for an investigation. [Source: Section 94, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Summons to produce document or other thing

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 94: Summons to produce document or other thing

Q: What does Section 94 of BNSS 2023 establish?
A: Section 94 of BNSS 2023 establishes the power of courts and police station heads to compel the production of physical documents and digital evidence (like phones) from individuals holding them. [Source: Section 94, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Summons to produce document or other thing

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 94: Summons to produce document or other thing

Q: A station chief sends a WhatsApp message ordering a company to produce its accounting ledgers. Is an electronic order valid for this purpose?
A: Yes, under sub-section (1), the officer may require production by a written order, "either in physical form or in electronic form." [Source: Section 94, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Summons to produce document or other thing

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 94: Summons to produce document or other thing

Q: What condition justifies the issuance of this summons or order?
A: The Court or officer must consider that the production is "necessary or desirable for the purposes of any investigation, inquiry, trial or other proceeding under this Sanhita." [Source: Section 94, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Summons to produce document or other thing

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 94: Summons to produce document or other thing

Q: If a person is ordered to produce a document, do they have to go to court and hand it over personally?
A: No, under sub-section (2), they are deemed to have complied if they "causes such document or thing to be produced instead of attending personally to produce the same." [Source: Section 94, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Summons to produce document or other thing

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 94: Summons to produce document or other thing

Q: What is the consequence of this section regarding postal letters?
A: The consequence is that this section cannot be used to seize mail; sub-section (3) explicitly states nothing in this section shall "apply to a letter, postcard... in the custody of the postal authority." [Source: Section 94, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Summons to produce document or other thing

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 95: Procedure as to letters

Q: How can authorities get access to a suspect's mail held at the post office?
A: The District Magistrate, Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court of Session, or High Court can order the postal authority to deliver the document or parcel to a directed person. [Source: Section 95, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Procedure as to letters

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 95: Procedure as to letters

Q: What is Section 95 of BNSS 2023 about?
A: Section 95 of BNSS 2023 outlines the specialized procedure for compelling postal authorities to surrender letters and parcels, distinguishing between the powers of higher courts to order delivery and lower magistrates/police to order detention. [Source: Section 95, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Procedure as to letters

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 95: Procedure as to letters

Q: A Superintendent of Police learns a bomb component is in a parcel at the local post office. They order the postmaster to immediately hand it over to them. Does the Superintendent have this power under this section?
A: No, under sub-section (2), the Superintendent may only require the postal authority to "detain such document, parcel or thing pending the order" of a higher Magistrate. Only higher courts can order actual delivery. [Source: Section 95, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Procedure as to letters

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 95: Procedure as to letters

Q: Which specific judicial authorities have the power to actually require the postal authority to deliver the parcel under sub-section (1)?
A: Only the "District Magistrate, Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court of Session or High Court." [Source: Section 95, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Procedure as to letters

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 95: Procedure as to letters

Q: Can a regular Executive Magistrate order the post office to search for and hold a letter?
A: Yes, under sub-section (2), "any other Magistrate, whether Executive or Judicial" can require the postal authority to "cause search to be made for and to detain" the item. [Source: Section 95, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Procedure as to letters

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 95: Procedure as to letters

Q: What is the consequence of this section for the privacy of postal communications?
A: The consequence is that the privacy of mail is strongly protected, as only the highest-ranking Magistrates and Courts are granted the statutory power to breach postal custody and seize communications. [Source: Section 95, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Procedure as to letters

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 96: When search-warrant may be issued

Q: Under what circumstances can a court issue a search warrant for a place?
A: A Court may issue a search warrant if it believes a person will not produce a required document, if the document's location is unknown, or if a general search serves the purposes of an inquiry or trial. [Source: Section 96, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: When search-warrant may be issued

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 96: When search-warrant may be issued

Q: What does Section 96 of BNSS 2023 establish?
A: Section 96 of BNSS 2023 establishes the three core conditions under which a court is authorized to issue a search warrant, and outlines its ability to restrict the search to specific areas. [Source: Section 96, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: When search-warrant may be issued

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 96: When search-warrant may be issued

Q: A judge wants to find a murder weapon but has no idea who has it or where it is. Can the judge issue a search warrant?
A: Yes, under clause (b), a warrant can be issued if "such document or thing is not known to the Court to be in the possession of any person." [Source: Section 96, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: When search-warrant may be issued

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 96: When search-warrant may be issued

Q: What is the condition for issuing a warrant based on a person's anticipated refusal?
A: The condition is that the Court "has reason to believe that a person... will not or would not produce the document or thing as required by such summons or requisition." [Source: Section 96, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: When search-warrant may be issued

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 96: When search-warrant may be issued

Q: If a warrant is issued for a house, can police rip open every wall and floorboard automatically?
A: Not necessarily; under sub-section (2), the Court may "specify in the warrant the particular place or part thereof to which only the search or inspection shall extend." [Source: Section 96, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: When search-warrant may be issued

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 96: When search-warrant may be issued

Q: What is the limitation placed on ordinary Magistrates regarding searches of the postal system?
A: The consequence of sub-section (3) is a strict limitation: nothing in this section authorizes any Magistrate other than a "District Magistrate or Chief Judicial Magistrate" to grant a warrant to search postal custody. [Source: Section 96, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: When search-warrant may be issued

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 97: Search of place suspected to contain stolen property, forged documents, etc

Q: Can police get a warrant to search a warehouse they suspect is being used to store fake currency or stolen goods?
A: Yes, a District Magistrate, Sub-divisional Magistrate, or Magistrate of the first class may authorize a police officer above the rank of constable to enter and search such a place and seize objectionable articles. [Source: Section 97, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search of place suspected to contain stolen property, forged documents, etc

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 97: Search of place suspected to contain stolen property, forged documents, etc

Q: What is Section 97 of BNSS 2023 about?
A: Section 97 of BNSS 2023 grants specific Magistrates the power to issue warrants to raid locations suspected of harboring stolen property or producing illicit items like counterfeit money, forged documents, and obscene objects. [Source: Section 97, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search of place suspected to contain stolen property, forged documents, etc

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 97: Search of place suspected to contain stolen property, forged documents, etc

Q: A Magistrate issues a warrant under this section and directs it to a local constable to execute the raid. Is this lawful?
A: No, the section explicitly states the Magistrate may by warrant authorize "any police officer above the rank of a constable" to execute these specialized searches. [Source: Section 97, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search of place suspected to contain stolen property, forged documents, etc

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 97: Search of place suspected to contain stolen property, forged documents, etc

Q: What are three examples of "objectionable articles" listed in sub-section (2)?
A: The list includes "(a) counterfeit coin; (c) counterfeit currency note; counterfeit stamps; (d) forged documents." [Source: Section 97, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search of place suspected to contain stolen property, forged documents, etc

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 97: Search of place suspected to contain stolen property, forged documents, etc

Q: Does the warrant only allow the officer to seize the physical stolen items?
A: No, it also authorizes them "to take into custody and carry before a Magistrate every person found in such place" who appears privy to the deposit, sale, or production of the items. [Source: Section 97, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search of place suspected to contain stolen property, forged documents, etc

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 97: Search of place suspected to contain stolen property, forged documents, etc

Q: What is the legal consequence for a property owner if their premises are used to store materials for making fake seals?
A: The consequence is that their premises are subject to forceful entry and search under this section, as sub-section (2)(g) includes "instruments or materials used for the production of any of the articles mentioned" as objectionable. [Source: Section 97, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search of place suspected to contain stolen property, forged documents, etc

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 98: Power to declare certain publications forfeited and to issue search-warrants for

Q: Can the government ban a book and order police to seize every copy of it?
A: Yes, if a publication contains punishable matter, the State Government may declare every copy forfeited to the Government, and Magistrates may authorize police to search premises for them. [Source: Section 98, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to declare certain publications forfeited and to issue search-warrants for

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 98: Power to declare certain publications forfeited and to issue search-warrants for

Q: What does Section 98 of BNSS 2023 state?
A: Section 98 of BNSS 2023 states the State Government's power to forfeit publications containing severe criminal offenses (like inciting violence or obscenity) and authorizes widespread police searches to confiscate those documents. [Source: Section 98, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to declare certain publications forfeited and to issue search-warrants for

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 98: Power to declare certain publications forfeited and to issue search-warrants for

Q: The State Government bans a highly offensive painting. Can a constable be authorized by a Magistrate to search a gallery for it?
A: No, sub-section (1) requires the Magistrate to authorize "any police officer not below the rank of sub-inspector" to enter and search for such documents. [Source: Section 98, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to declare certain publications forfeited and to issue search-warrants for

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 98: Power to declare certain publications forfeited and to issue search-warrants for

Q: What procedural requirement must the State Government fulfill when issuing the notification of forfeiture?
A: The State Government must issue the notification "stating the grounds of its opinion." [Source: Section 98, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to declare certain publications forfeited and to issue search-warrants for

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 98: Power to declare certain publications forfeited and to issue search-warrants for

Q: Does the term "document" in this section only mean printed text like books and newspapers?
A: No, sub-section (2)(b) states that "document" includes "any painting, drawing or photograph, or other visible representation." [Source: Section 98, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to declare certain publications forfeited and to issue search-warrants for

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 98: Power to declare certain publications forfeited and to issue search-warrants for

Q: What is the jurisdictional consequence regarding civil courts trying to block this order?
A: The consequence, under sub-section (3), is that "No order passed or action taken under this section shall be called in question in any Court" except as provided in section 99. [Source: Section 98, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to declare certain publications forfeited and to issue search-warrants for

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 99: Application to High Court to set aside declaration of forfeiture

Q: If the government bans a book, can the author challenge that ban in court?
A: Yes, any person having an interest in the forfeited publication may apply to the High Court within two months of the declaration to have it set aside. [Source: Section 99, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Application to High Court to set aside declaration of forfeiture

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 99: Application to High Court to set aside declaration of forfeiture

Q: What is Section 99 of BNSS 2023 about?
A: Section 99 of BNSS 2023 outlines the appellate remedy for state-mandated forfeitures, allowing interested parties to petition a Special Bench of the High Court to overturn the ban. [Source: Section 99, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Application to High Court to set aside declaration of forfeiture

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 99: Application to High Court to set aside declaration of forfeiture

Q: An author waits three months after the government gazettes the ban on their book to file a petition in the High Court. Will the court hear it?
A: No, under sub-section (1), the application must be made "within two months from the date of publication in the Official Gazette of such declaration." [Source: Section 99, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Application to High Court to set aside declaration of forfeiture

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 99: Application to High Court to set aside declaration of forfeiture

Q: What specific argument must the applicant make to successfully overturn the declaration?
A: They must argue that the publication "did not contain any such matter as is referred to in sub-section (1) of section 98." [Source: Section 99, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Application to High Court to set aside declaration of forfeiture

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 99: Application to High Court to set aside declaration of forfeiture

Q: Can a single High Court judge decide this matter?
A: No, sub-section (2) states it shall be heard by "a Special Bench of the High Court composed of three Judges" (or all judges if the court has fewer than three). [Source: Section 99, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Application to High Court to set aside declaration of forfeiture

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 99: Application to High Court to set aside declaration of forfeiture

Q: What is the consequence if the three judges on the Special Bench disagree on whether the book is punishable?
A: The consequence, under sub-section (5), is that "the decision shall be in accordance with the opinion of the majority of those Judges." [Source: Section 99, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Application to High Court to set aside declaration of forfeiture

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 100: Search for persons wrongfully confined

Q: If someone is being held hostage or illegally imprisoned in a house, can a magistrate issue a search warrant to rescue them?
A: Yes, if a Magistrate has reason to believe a person is wrongfully confined, they may issue a search warrant, and the person executing it may search for the confined individual and bring them before the Magistrate. [Source: Section 100, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search for persons wrongfully confined

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 100: Search for persons wrongfully confined

Q: What does Section 100 of BNSS 2023 state?
A: Section 100 of BNSS 2023 provides Magistrates with the authority to issue warrants specifically to search for and rescue victims of wrongful confinement, effectively acting as an emergency habeas corpus mechanism at the local level. [Source: Section 100, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search for persons wrongfully confined

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 100: Search for persons wrongfully confined

Q: An officer executes a search warrant for a kidnapped child, finds the child, and immediately takes them back to their parents. Did the officer follow the exact procedure?
A: No, the section requires that "the person, if found, shall be immediately taken before a Magistrate, who shall make such order as in the circumstances of the case seems proper." [Source: Section 100, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search for persons wrongfully confined

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 100: Search for persons wrongfully confined

Q: What level of belief must the Magistrate possess to issue this specific warrant?
A: The Magistrate must have "reason to believe that any person is confined under such circumstances that the confinement amounts to an offence." [Source: Section 100, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search for persons wrongfully confined

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 100: Search for persons wrongfully confined

Q: Can a Second Class Magistrate issue this type of rescue warrant?
A: No, the power is explicitly granted only to "any District Magistrate, Sub-divisional Magistrate or Magistrate of the first class." [Source: Section 100, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search for persons wrongfully confined

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 100: Search for persons wrongfully confined

Q: What is the consequence once the rescued individual is brought before the Magistrate?
A: The consequence is that the Magistrate assumes immediate legal control over the victim's welfare, empowered to "make such order as in the circumstances of the case seems proper" to ensure their safety and liberty. [Source: Section 100, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Search for persons wrongfully confined

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 101: Power to compel restoration of abducted females

Q: Can a magistrate order police to forcibly rescue a kidnapped woman and return her to her family?
A: Yes, upon a complaint made on oath, a Magistrate may make an order for the immediate restoration of an abducted woman to her liberty, or a female child to her parent/guardian, using necessary force. [Source: Section 101, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to compel restoration of abducted females

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 101: Power to compel restoration of abducted females

Q: What is the purpose of Section 101 of BNSS 2023?
A: Section 101 of BNSS 2023 provides a direct, forceful legal mechanism for Magistrates to mandate the immediate rescue and restoration of abducted women and female children held for unlawful purposes. [Source: Section 101, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to compel restoration of abducted females

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 101: Power to compel restoration of abducted females

Q: A father calls the police station and verbally claims his daughter was abducted. Can the Magistrate immediately issue a restoration order based solely on that phone call?
A: No, the section requires the action to be taken "Upon complaint made on oath of the abduction or unlawful detention." [Source: Section 101, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to compel restoration of abducted females

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 101: Power to compel restoration of abducted females

Q: Who must a female child be restored to under this section?
A: She must be restored "to her parent, guardian or other person having the lawful charge of such child." [Source: Section 101, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to compel restoration of abducted females

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 101: Power to compel restoration of abducted females

Q: Are the authorities limited to just asking nicely for the victim's return?
A: No, the Magistrate "may compel compliance with such order, using such force as may be necessary." [Source: Section 101, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to compel restoration of abducted females

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 101: Power to compel restoration of abducted females

Q: What is the legal consequence for an adult woman successfully rescued under this order?
A: The consequence is "the immediate restoration of such woman to her liberty," granting her immediate freedom from the unlawful detention. [Source: Section 101, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power to compel restoration of abducted females

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 102: Direction, etc., of search-warrants

Q: Do the rules for executing arrest warrants also apply to search warrants?
A: Yes, the provisions of several sections governing arrest warrants (like sections 32, 72, 74, 76, 79, 80 and 81) apply, so far as may be, to search-warrants issued under sections 96, 97, 98 or 100. [Source: Section 102, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Direction, etc., of search-warrants

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 102: Direction, etc., of search-warrants

Q: What does Section 102 of BNSS 2023 dictate?
A: Section 102 of BNSS 2023 dictates that the general procedural rules regarding the direction and execution of arrest warrants also govern the execution of search warrants. [Source: Section 102, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Direction, etc., of search-warrants

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 102: Direction, etc., of search-warrants

Q: A lawyer argues that a search warrant was executed improperly because it was sent by post to an outside jurisdiction, claiming that rule only applies to arrest warrants. Is the lawyer correct?
A: No, Section 102 explicitly makes the provisions of Section 80 (which allows forwarding warrants outside jurisdiction) applicable "to all search-warrants issued under section 96, section 97, section 98 or section 100." [Source: Section 102, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Direction, etc., of search-warrants

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 102: Direction, etc., of search-warrants

Q: What is the functional consequence of this cross-referencing section?
A: The consequence is that it streamlines the Sanhita by applying established procedural mechanics (like who executes a warrant and jurisdictional boundaries) equally to both arrests and property searches. [Source: Section 102, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Direction, etc., of search-warrants

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 102: Direction, etc., of search-warrants

Q: Does this section apply to a restoration order made under Section 101?
A: No, the section explicitly applies the listed rules only "to all search-warrants issued under section 96, section 97, section 98 or section 100." [Source: Section 102, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Direction, etc., of search-warrants

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 102: Direction, etc., of search-warrants

Q: To which specific search warrant sections do these rules apply?
A: They apply to search-warrants issued under "section 96, section 97, section 98 or section 100." [Source: Section 102, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Direction, etc., of search-warrants

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 103: Persons in charge of closed place to allow search

Q: If police show up with a search warrant, do you have to let them into your house?
A: Yes, any person residing in or in charge of a closed place must, on demand and production of the warrant, allow free ingress and afford all reasonable facilities for a search. [Source: Section 103, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Persons in charge of closed place to allow search

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 103: Persons in charge of closed place to allow search

Q: What is Section 103 of BNSS 2023 about?
A: Section 103 of BNSS 2023 outlines the procedures for conducting searches of closed places, mandating occupant cooperation, requiring independent witnesses, and ensuring the occupant receives a list of seized items. [Source: Section 103, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Persons in charge of closed place to allow search

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 103: Persons in charge of closed place to allow search

Q: An officer conducts a search without calling any witnesses. They seize evidence. Was the search procedure legally compliant?
A: No, sub-section (4) mandates that before making a search, the officer "shall call upon two or more independent and respectable inhabitants of the locality... to attend and witness the search." [Source: Section 103, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Persons in charge of closed place to allow search

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 103: Persons in charge of closed place to allow search

Q: What right does the occupant of the searched place have during the process?
A: Under sub-section (6), the occupant "shall, in every instance, be permitted to attend during the search, and a copy of the list prepared under this section... shall be delivered to such occupant." [Source: Section 103, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Persons in charge of closed place to allow search

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 103: Persons in charge of closed place to allow search

Q: Can an officer search the physical body of a person found at the location?
A: Yes, under sub-section (3), if any person is reasonably suspected of concealing an article on their person, "such person may be searched." If it's a woman, the search must be made by another woman. [Source: Section 103, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Persons in charge of closed place to allow search

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 103: Persons in charge of closed place to allow search

Q: What is the penal consequence for a citizen who refuses to act as a witness to a search after receiving a written order?
A: The consequence is that they "shall be deemed to have committed an offence under section 222 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023." [Source: Section 103, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Persons in charge of closed place to allow search

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 104: Disposal of things found in search beyond jurisdiction

Q: What should be done with items found during an out-of-jurisdiction search?
A: The things found, along with a prepared list, must be immediately taken to the Court that issued the warrant, unless the place is nearer to the local Magistrate, in which case they go to the Magistrate first. [Source: Section 104, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Disposal of things found in search beyond jurisdiction

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 104: Disposal of things found in search beyond jurisdiction

Q: What does Section 104 of BNSS 2023 specify?
A: Section 104 of BNSS 2023 specifies the procedure for disposing of things found during the execution of a search warrant beyond the local jurisdiction of the issuing Court. [Source: Section 104, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Disposal of things found in search beyond jurisdiction

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 104: Disposal of things found in search beyond jurisdiction

Q: Police execute a search warrant in a neighbouring district and find the stolen goods. The local Magistrate's office is right down the street, while the issuing Court is 50 kilometers away. Where should they take the goods first?
A: They should take the goods and the list immediately to the local Magistrate, because the place of search is nearer to the Magistrate having jurisdiction therein than to the issuing Court. [Source: Section 104, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Disposal of things found in search beyond jurisdiction

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 104: Disposal of things found in search beyond jurisdiction

Q: What must accompany the things found when they are taken to the Court or Magistrate?
A: The things found must be accompanied by "the list of the same prepared under the provisions hereinafter contained." [Source: Section 104, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Disposal of things found in search beyond jurisdiction

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 104: Disposal of things found in search beyond jurisdiction

Q: Under what condition will the local Magistrate not authorize taking the things to the issuing Court?
A: The Magistrate shall make an order authorizing them to be taken to the issuing Court "unless there be good cause to the contrary." [Source: Section 104, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Disposal of things found in search beyond jurisdiction

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 104: Disposal of things found in search beyond jurisdiction

Q: What is the required action of the local Magistrate once the items are brought before them?
A: The consequence is that the Magistrate must "make an order authorising them to be taken to such Court" which issued the warrant, barring good cause to the contrary. [Source: Section 104, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Disposal of things found in search beyond jurisdiction

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 105: Recording of search and seizure through audio-video electronic means

Q: Is it mandatory for police to record a search operation on video?
A: Yes, the process of conducting a search or taking possession of property, including the preparation and signing of the seizure list, shall be recorded through audio-video electronic means, preferably a mobile phone. [Source: Section 105, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Recording of search and seizure through audio-video electronic means

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 105: Recording of search and seizure through audio-video electronic means

Q: What does Section 105 of BNSS 2023 mandate?
A: Section 105 of BNSS 2023 mandates that the entire process of search and seizure, including preparing and signing the seizure list, must be recorded using audio-video electronic means. [Source: Section 105, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Recording of search and seizure through audio-video electronic means

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 105: Recording of search and seizure through audio-video electronic means

Q: A police officer films a house search on his mobile phone and captures the signing of the seizure list. He keeps the video on his phone for a month until trial. Is this the correct procedure?
A: No, the section requires that the police officer shall "without delay forward such recording to the District Magistrate, Sub-divisional Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the first class." [Source: Section 105, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Recording of search and seizure through audio-video electronic means

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 105: Recording of search and seizure through audio-video electronic means

Q: What specific parts of the search process must be included in the audio-video recording?
A: The recording must include the "process of conducting search of a place or taking possession of any property, article or thing," as well as the "preparation of the list of all things seized" and the "signing of such list by witnesses." [Source: Section 105, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Recording of search and seizure through audio-video electronic means

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 105: Recording of search and seizure through audio-video electronic means

Q: Who are the three specific officials to whom the recording can be forwarded?
A: The recording must be forwarded to the "District Magistrate, Sub-divisional Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the first class." [Source: Section 105, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Recording of search and seizure through audio-video electronic means

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 105: Recording of search and seizure through audio-video electronic means

Q: What is the practical result of this section on how police document seizures?
A: The consequence is that traditional paper-only seizure lists are no longer sufficient on their own; they must be corroborated by an audio-video recording, preferably via mobile phone, forwarded promptly to a Magistrate. [Source: Section 105, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Recording of search and seizure through audio-video electronic means

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 106: Power of police officer to seize certain property

Q: When can a police officer seize property without a warrant?
A: A police officer may seize any property which is alleged or suspected to have been stolen, or which is found under circumstances creating suspicion of the commission of any offence. [Source: Section 106, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power of police officer to seize certain property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 106: Power of police officer to seize certain property

Q: What authority does Section 106 of BNSS 2023 grant?
A: Section 106 of BNSS 2023 grants police officers the power to seize suspected stolen property or property found under suspicious circumstances, and outlines the reporting and custody procedures for such seizures. [Source: Section 106, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power of police officer to seize certain property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 106: Power of police officer to seize certain property

Q: A constable seizes a suspected stolen bicycle but it is too cumbersome to transport to the Court. What can the officer do with it?
A: Under sub-section (3), the officer may give custody of the bicycle to any person upon their executing a bond undertaking to produce the property before the Court as required. [Source: Section 106, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power of police officer to seize certain property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 106: Power of police officer to seize certain property

Q: Under sub-section (3), under what three conditions can an officer release seized property on a bond rather than taking it to Court?
A: The property can be released on a bond if it "cannot be conveniently transported to the Court," if there is "difficulty in securing proper accommodation for the custody," or if "continued retention of the property in police custody may not be considered necessary for the purpose of investigation." [Source: Section 106, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power of police officer to seize certain property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 106: Power of police officer to seize certain property

Q: Can police immediately sell seized property without waiting for a court order?
A: Yes, under the proviso, if the property is subject to speedy and natural decay, the owner is unknown or absent, and its value is less than five hundred rupees, it may be sold forthwith by auction under the orders of the Superintendent of Police. [Source: Section 106, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power of police officer to seize certain property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 106: Power of police officer to seize certain property

Q: What is the reporting consequence for a subordinate police officer who seizes property under this section?
A: Under sub-section (2), a subordinate police officer "shall forthwith report the seizure to that officer" in charge of the police station. [Source: Section 106, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Power of police officer to seize certain property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 107: Attachment, forfeiture or restoration of property

Q: How can police freeze assets that they believe were bought with crime money?
A: An investigating officer, with the approval of the Superintendent or Commissioner of Police, can apply to the Court or Magistrate to attach property believed to be derived from a criminal activity or offence. [Source: Section 107, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Attachment, forfeiture or restoration of property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 107: Attachment, forfeiture or restoration of property

Q: What does Section 107 of BNSS 2023 establish?
A: Section 107 of BNSS 2023 establishes the mechanism for the attachment and forfeiture of proceeds of crime, and provides for the rateable distribution of these funds to the victims of the offence. [Source: Section 107, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Attachment, forfeiture or restoration of property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 107: Attachment, forfeiture or restoration of property

Q: The Magistrate believes giving a suspect a 14-day notice about attaching their bank account will cause the suspect to immediately transfer the money away. Can the Magistrate attach the account right away?
A: Yes, under sub-section (5), if issuing notice would defeat the object of attachment, the Magistrate may pass an interim ex parte order directing the attachment or seizure of such property. [Source: Section 107, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Attachment, forfeiture or restoration of property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 107: Attachment, forfeiture or restoration of property

Q: What steps must the Magistrate take before passing a final order of attachment under sub-section (4)?
A: The Magistrate must consider the explanation to the show-cause notice, consider available material facts, and give "a reasonable opportunity of being heard to such person or persons." [Source: Section 107, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Attachment, forfeiture or restoration of property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 107: Attachment, forfeiture or restoration of property

Q: If there are no victims or claimants to receive the seized proceeds of a crime, what happens to the money?
A: Under sub-section (8), if there are no claimants, no ascertainable claimant, or a surplus remains, "such proceeds of crime shall stand forfeited to the Government." [Source: Section 107, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Attachment, forfeiture or restoration of property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 107: Attachment, forfeiture or restoration of property

Q: What is the ultimate consequence for the victims once the Court finds the attached properties are indeed proceeds of crime?
A: Under sub-section (6), the Court shall order the District Magistrate to "rateably distribute such proceeds of crime to the persons who are affected by such crime." [Source: Section 107, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Attachment, forfeiture or restoration of property

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 108: Magistrate may direct search in his presence

Q: Can a Magistrate personally supervise a search?
A: Yes, any Magistrate may direct a search to be made in his presence at any place for which he has the authority to issue a search warrant. [Source: Section 108, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Magistrate may direct search in his presence

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 108: Magistrate may direct search in his presence

Q: What is the function of Section 108 of BNSS 2023?
A: Section 108 of BNSS 2023 authorizes a Magistrate to personally oversee and direct a physical search of a place, provided they are legally competent to issue a search warrant for that location. [Source: Section 108, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Magistrate may direct search in his presence

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 108: Magistrate may direct search in his presence

Q: A Magistrate wants to personally ensure a sensitive location is searched properly, but they do not have the jurisdiction to issue a search warrant for that specific building. Can they still direct the search in their presence?
A: No, the section limits this power to "any place for the search of which he is competent to issue a search-warrant." [Source: Section 108, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Magistrate may direct search in his presence

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 108: Magistrate may direct search in his presence

Q: What are the two key conditions for a Magistrate to exercise power under this section?
A: The Magistrate must "direct a search to be made in his presence" and the location must be a place "for the search of which he is competent to issue a search-warrant." [Source: Section 108, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Magistrate may direct search in his presence

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 108: Magistrate may direct search in his presence

Q: Who holds the authority to direct such an in-person search?
A: The authority is granted broadly to "Any Magistrate." [Source: Section 108, BNSS 2023]

metadata.section_title: Magistrate may direct search in his presence

content:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) - Section 108: Magistrate may direct search in his presence

Q: What is the procedural consequence of this section regarding the issuance of warrants?
A: The consequence is that a Magistrate can bypass the formal issuance of a written warrant to police if they choose to be physically present and direct the search themselves. [Source: Section 108, BNSS 2023]
